mathematical_checks.finding: C2 gives continuous gradient, hence joint continuous flow/rate and Borel reflection. Division by zero is the specified zero-safe real division; reflection is Borel even at vanishing normal. No joint continuity of reflection asserted.

For fixed center, each coordinate harmonic block is [[cos u,sqrt(eta)*sin u],[-sin u/sqrt(eta),cos u]], determinant cos(u)^2+sin(u)^2=1 because eta>0. In dimension d its determinant is 1^d, and translation preserves canonical volume. Explicit product volume matches orthonormal coordinate Lebesgue volume. All real u covered.

For fixed x, the momentum map is an orthogonal reflection when the normal is nonzero and identity when it is zero. Each fiber preserves canonical momentum volume. Joint Borel measurability and sigma-finiteness of finite-dimensional volume give preservation of position-times-momentum product measure. State dependence requires no differentiability or nonvanishing-normal assumption.
Position identity times momentum negation preserves the explicit product measure.

Flow inverse follows the harmonic group algebra; reflection squares to identity including zero normal; momentum negation is involutive. Negating momentum conjugates u-flow to (-u)-flow and commutes with the linear reflection at the unchanged position.

For every normal n and momentum p, <B(n,p),n>=-<p,n>, including n=0. Therefore <-B(n,p),n>=<p,n> and the same sqrt(eta)*positive-part rate is retained under R after S. No positive-rate or nonzero-normal premise is needed.

Measure-preserving pullback preserves AE strong measurability, integrability and the signed real integral. Integrable F is sufficient without a separate everywhere-measurable F binder. Boundedness alone would be insufficient on infinite phase volume; the header uses the correct hypothesis.

u=0 gives identity; arbitrary positive/negative u and arbitrary centers are valid.
eta=0 is excluded and must remain excluded for flow inverse/volume; no limiting eta=0 claim.
